prompt: coreutils chroot newroot identical old root directory behavior
answer:
When `NEWROOT` is identical to the old `/`, GNU Coreutils `chroot` **skips the `chroot` system call**. This is done for consistency with systems where using `chroot` this way is permitted for non-privileged users.

The command is still run normally; by default, `chroot` changes the working directory to `/`. The `--skip-chdir` option is permitted specifically when `NEWROOT` is the old `/` directory.

Source: [GNU Coreutils `chroot` invocation](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/html_node/chroot-invocation.html)
